senses.sense_definition: A person who creates or assigns names to things, especially within a scientific classification system.

examples.text: The <w>nomenclator</w> carefully chose a Latin term to describe the newly discovered species of beetle.
As a professional <w>nomenclator</w>, she ensures that all chemical compounds are named according to international standards.

senses.sense_definition: An assistant who reminds a person of the names of people they meet at social events.

examples.text: In ancient Rome, a wealthy politician would often employ a <w>nomenclator</w> to help him recognize his many supporters.
The <w>nomenclator</w> whispered the guest's name into the host's ear just before the introduction.

traits.comment: Refers to a historical social role.

senses.sense_definition: A document or list that contains a system of names or terms.

examples.text: The researchers consulted the <w>nomenclator</w> to ensure they were using the correct terminology for the project.
This technical <w>nomenclator</w> provides a standardized list of all parts used in the engine design.

senses.sense_definition: An early type of substitution cipher used for secret communication.

examples.text: Diplomats in the seventeenth century often used a <w>nomenclator</w> to encrypt their sensitive correspondence.
The historian discovered that the secret message was encoded using a complex <w>nomenclator</w>.

traits.comment: Refers to an obsolete method of encryption.
